title: Plum crumble
intro: Ripe plums turning jammy under a crisp topping of butter and oats.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Stone the plums, quarter them and toss them in a baking dish with sugar, cinnamon and cornstarch.
Rub flour, cubed butter, sugar, oats and salt together with your fingertips into coarse crumbs.
Scatter the crumble over the fruit without pressing it down.
Bake until the topping is golden and the fruit juices bubble at the edges.
steps.label: Bake

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 170 °C for 22 minutes in a dish that fits the basket, until golden.

steps.t: Let it rest out of the oven so the juices thicken.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Serve it warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
In autumn use apples and blackberries; in winter pears with a pinch of ginger.
Next day, reheat it for 10 minutes at 180 °C and the topping turns crisp again.

title: Pears poached in red wine
intro: Whole pears simmered slowly in spiced wine until ruby red.

steps.t: Peel the pears, leaving the stalk on, and trim a thin slice off the base so they stand up.
In a tall, narrow pan bring wine, sugar, cinnamon, cloves and orange peel to the boil.
Stand the pears upright in the wine, close together.
Cover and simmer gently, basting often, until a skewer slides in easily.
steps.label: Pears

steps.t: Lift out the pears and boil the wine hard until it is a syrup that coats a spoon.
steps.label: Syrup

steps.t: Serve the pears warm or cold, drizzled with the syrup.

tips.t: Serve them with a spoonful of mascarpone or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Left overnight in the syrup in the fridge, they turn red right to the core.

title: Summer fruit salad
intro: Peaches, melon, apricots and blueberries in their own juice, with lemon and mint.

steps.t: Squeeze the lemon into a large bowl and dissolve the sugar in the juice.
Peel and deseed the melon and cut it into 1.5 cm cubes.
Dice the peaches and apricots and toss them straight into the lemon juice so they don't brown.
Add the melon, blueberries and torn mint and stir gently.
Cover and chill: the fruit releases its juice.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Serve it well chilled in small bowls, with its syrup.

tips.t: Top it with a scoop of lemon sorbet for a summer dinner dessert.
Use the juice of an orange instead of sugar: fresher and less sweet.

title: Tarte tatin
intro: Upside-down apple tart: whole wedges in butter caramel under a disc of shortcrust.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel, quarter and core the apples.
In a 24 cm ovenproof frying pan melt the sugar over medium heat, without stirring, until amber.
Take off the heat and stir in the butter in pieces and the salt: watch out for spatters.
Stand the apple quarters upright, packed tight, and cook over medium heat until the caramel bubbles thickly.
steps.label: Apples

steps.t: Roll the pastry (shop-bought is fine) into a 26 cm disc, lay it over the apples and tuck the edges inside.
Prick the pastry and bake until puffed and golden.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Rest it for a few minutes, no longer, so the caramel doesn't set.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Cover with a larger plate, flip it over in one confident move and put back any apples that stuck.

tips.t: Serve it warm with a spoonful of cold crème fraîche or sour cream.
Pick apples that hold their shape, like russets: watery apples give a runny caramel.
Use firm pears and a pinch of ginger for a winter version.

title: Mango sticky rice
intro: Coconut sticky rice, ripe mango and a salty-sweet sauce: the Thai street dessert.

steps.t: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and leave it to soak in cold water.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Drain it and steam it in a basket lined with a cloth until translucent and tender.
steps.label: Steam

steps.t: Meanwhile warm 250 ml of the coconut milk with 50 g sugar and half the salt, without boiling, until dissolved.
Tip the hot rice into the sweet coconut milk, stir, cover and let it soak it up.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Heat the rest of the coconut milk with the remaining sugar and salt and the cornstarch slaked in water, until it coats a spoon.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Peel the mangoes and slice the flesh off the stone.
Serve the warm rice next to the mango, spoon over the sauce and sprinkle with sesame.

tips.t: You need Thai glutinous rice: regular rice won't turn sticky or absorb the coconut.
The rice hardens in the fridge: microwave it covered for 30 seconds before serving.

title: Kluai buat chi, bananas in coconut milk
intro: Bananas gently poached in coconut milk with palm sugar and a pinch of salt.

steps.t: Peel the bananas, halve them lengthwise, then cut into 5 cm pieces.
In a saucepan warm the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Don't let it boil hard.
Add the bananas and simmer gently for 6 minutes, until soft and slightly translucent but still whole.
steps.label: Bananas

steps.t: Turn off the heat and let it rest 5 minutes so the bananas soak up the coconut.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Taste: it should be sweet with a salty edge. Serve warm in small bowls.

tips.t: Look for kluai nam wa in Thai shops, small firm bananas that hold their shape and turn slightly pink.
Swap the bananas for diced pumpkin and you get fak thong kaeng buat, its twin dessert.

title: Cinnamon oranges, Moroccan style
intro: Sliced oranges with orange blossom and cinnamon: the fresh finish after a tagine.

steps.t: Peel the oranges with a sharp knife, cutting away all the white pith.
Slice them into 5 mm rounds, remove the seeds and overlap them on a serving plate with their juice.
Sprinkle with the orange blossom water and dust with powdered sugar.
Cover and chill for 30 minutes, until nicely cold.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Just before serving, dust with cinnamon and scatter with the mint leaves.

tips.t: Add the cinnamon at the last moment: on the juice it turns damp and loses its scent.
Chopped dates and toasted almonds make it a richer dessert.
End the meal with a glass of hot mint tea.

title: Apple pie
intro: Flaky double crust and a tall filling of cinnamon apples: America's signature dessert.

ing.n: apples (half Granny Smith, half Golden Delicious)

steps.t: Peel and core the apples and cut them into 5 mm slices.
Toss with the sugar (save 1 tbsp), brown sugar, lemon juice and zest, spices, salt and cornstarch.
steps.label: Apples

steps.t: Meanwhile heat the oven to 200 °C and line a 23 cm pie dish with one disc of pastry (shop-bought is fine), letting it overhang.
Pile in the apples in a dome, leaving excess juice in the bowl, and dot with the butter.
Cover with the second disc, crimp the edges to seal and cut 4 slits in the centre to let steam escape.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with the reserved sugar and bake on the lowest shelf.
steps.label: Bake 200

steps.t: Lower to 180 °C and bake until deep golden and the juices bubble through the slits; shield the edges with foil if they darken.
steps.label: Bake 180

steps.t: Let it cool on a wire rack: the filling sets and the slices hold their shape.
steps.label: Cooling

tips.t: Serve it à la mode: a warm slice with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Lattice top: cut the second disc into 2 cm strips and weave them over the apples.
Bake the pie on a preheated baking tray: the base crisps up and any juice won't drip onto the oven.
